lŏcū^plēto , āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. locuples,
I.to make rich, enrich (syn. dito).
I. Lit.: auro suas domus, Att. ap. Gell. 14, 1, 34: “homines fortunis,” Cic. Agr. 2, 26 : “maxima auri argentique praeda locupletatus,” id. Rep. 2, 24, 44 ; id. Verr. 2, 5, 31, § 80: “Africam equis, armis, viris, pecunia,” Nep. Hamilc. 4, 1 : “cives,” Cic. Rep. 2, 9, 15 : “celeriter locupletari,” to grow rich, Col. 6 praef. § 4.—
II. Trop., to enrich, etc.: “sapientem locupletat ipsa natura,” Cic. Fin. 2, 28, 90 : “ipsam eloquentiam graviorum artium instrumento,” id. Brut. 97, 331 : “templum picturis,” i. e. to decorate, adorn, id. Inv. 2, 1 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
